executive_assessment.text: Provincial climate impacts and household vulnerability differ, with water, sanitation and food poverty shaping sensitivity in named provinces.
Cape Winelands evidence identifies De Doorns, Touwsrivier and Witzenberg vulnerabilities, but the indicators are dated and future risks are modeled.

National mandates, municipal prioritization and community organizations provide an adaptation-readiness picture, not proof of delivered outcomes. Historical weather-crime associations remain causally and geographically bounded.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2025-10 reports: The NDC reports recent floods in KwaZulu-Natal, Eastern and Western Cape; Northern Cape/interior heatwaves; droughts in Eastern Cape, Western Cape and Free State; Gauteng storms and Western Cape wildfires. Poor communities suffered most; businesses and municipalities struggled to recover.

Source dated 2025-10 reports: The NDC identifies high household climate vulnerability in KwaZulu-Natal, North West, Limpopo and Eastern Cape; eastern Eastern Cape municipalities are more vulnerable. Unsafe water/toilet access and food poverty are prominent.
Source dated 2023-07 reports: De Doorns and Touwsrivier score very high socioeconomic vulnerability; Touwsrivier also ranks worst for Breede Valley connectivity.
Source dated 2023-07 reports: Under RCP 8.5, increased future flood risk is projected for Paarl, Stellenbosch, De Doorns, Touwsrivier and Montagu.
Source dated 2023-07 reports: The profile's 2017-based table gives Witzenberg demand of 146.71 litres per capita daily against 144.23 supply, with a vulnerability score of 1.02.
Source dated 2023-07 reports: Witzenberg's water vulnerability score is projected to rise to 1.7 by 2050 with population pressure, declining rainfall and runoff, and increased evaporation.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 13 of 13 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.

No country-specific source-stated climate-change-to-organized-conflict or conflict-to-adaptation-constraint pathway was verified. The accessible crime study concerns weather and crime, not anthropogenic climate attribution.

A 2024 South Africa Biennial Transparency Report and two relevant World Bank PDFs were discoverable, but direct PDF reading failed at the web reader's 10 MiB limit; indexed passages were not used as evidence.

The most granular local vulnerability profile found was for Cape Winelands; it relies on dated 1996/2011 social indicators, 2017 water data and modeled future risk, so it does not provide a current nationwide municipal comparison.
